policy.renderGroupId: operator + official N02/GTFS line name (the package lineId with its -2/-3/-p1 geometry-part suffixes stripped)
why: rules.md §5.2: a route-preserving network keeps every named route in its own render group even where it shares track, and §5.5 forbids a hex colour from being the group id. Japan needs that profile network-wide, not per operator: japan_parallel_rail_rendering_rules.md states the identity of a DisplayLine is its public map name, and records that one operator repeats one colour across many lines, so colour cannot carry identity here at all.

Measured on this package: 小田急電鉄, 阪神電気鉄道 and 京浜急行電鉄 each paint EVERY one of their lines a single hex, and 京王電鉄 paints six. The North American default (operator + published colour) would collapse each of those operators' whole network onto one stroke. The Japan profile therefore keys on operator + official line name and never on colour.
byLineId is used for exactly one thing here — de-duplicating the geometry-part variants of ONE railway (the -2/-3/-p1 rows). It never merges two published lines.

evidence.name: Colour-collision census over jp-2025.json's 652 lines (this session)
evidence.detail: By operator: JR九州 29 lines/7 colours, 100% of colours shared by ≥2 lines; JR東日本 95 lines/55 colours, 16 colour-groups shared; 東武鉄道 13/9 colours, 4 groups (incl. 3-way #ed1a3d across 佐野線/小泉線/桐生線, lines that never touch); 近畿日本鉄道 24/17 colours, 7 groups; 名古屋鉄道 20/13 colours, 7 groups; 西武鉄道 12/9, 3 groups (incl. #ee5f00 across 6 lines); 小田急電鉄 3/1 (all three lines share one hex); 阪神電気鉄道 4/1 (all four); 京浜急行電鉄 5/1 (all five). By contrast every subway operator sampled (東京メトロ, 東京都, Osaka Metro, 京都市, 福岡市, 仙台市) publishes a near-distinct colour per line — subways are not the reason this policy exists, JR/private commuter branding is.

familiesConsidered.decision: not merged — kept route-preserving (two parallel lanes)
familiesConsidered.why: The audit itself flags this pair as needing an explicit profile decision (01_截图出现线路逐条规则.csv, 京王線 row): '新宿—笹塚一带京王线与京王新线为两条走向，并在笹塚汇合；是否作为独立RenderKey必须由Japan profile显式决定。' Two points argue against a trunk-family merge: (1) the audit's own wording describes them as '两条走向' (two distinct alignments) that converge at Sasazuka, i.e. a lane-count-decrease junction event (rules.md §9.3), not a single shared spine (§8.1) — they run on physically separate double-track alignments between Shinjuku and Sasazuka, unlike NYC's route-letter trunk collapse where the letters genuinely share one track. (2) Rule 3.1 and general-rules R-03 both explicitly forbid merging same-operator-same-colour lines by default; 京王線 and 京王新線 share #dd0077 with four other Keio lines (動物園線, 相模原線, 競馬場線, 高尾線), so a merge here would need to be justified as a real trunk-collapse, and the audit's own phrasing argues the opposite. Kept as two DisplayLines/render groups; jp-shared-measured.csv confirms 4 more short coincident/parallel spans between 京王線 and its other same-colour branches (相模原線, 動物園線, 競馬場線, 高尾線 — all under 500m, all at the stations where those branches meet the trunk), consistent with normal branch-junction behaviour rather than a merge case.
familiesConsidered.confidence: B — resolves the audit's own flagged ambiguity using the doc's stated rules, but is not independently confirmed against an Apple Maps capture at Sasazuka.

familiesConsidered.why: Unlike Keio, the audit's per-line rule text for every 東武鉄道 and 近畿日本鉄道 line (04_分岔合流逐线审计.csv, 01_截图出现线路逐条规则.csv) never uses the '必须由Japan profile显式決定' escalation language that flags 京王線 — searched the full audit text for that phrase and it appears exactly once, on the Keio row. Tobu and Kintetsu do reuse colour heavily across branches (Tobu: 4 colour groups across 13 lines; Kintetsu: 7 groups across 24 lines; see sameOperatorColourCollisionEvidence below), which is exactly why the default renderGroupId formula was changed to operator+name rather than operator+colour — but that is the general-policy fix, not a signal that any specific Tobu or Kintetsu branch pair should be collapsed into one lane. No coincident/parallel interval in jp-shared-measured.csv for a same-colour Tobu or Kintetsu pair runs longer than ~840m (東武 宇都宮線/日光線 at 744m; 近鉄 名古屋線/鈴鹿線 at 537m), i.e. junction-length touches, not multi-km shared trunks.

notInPackage.why: A JR East cross-Tokyo through-service pattern over the legal 東海道線/山手貨物線/赤羽線/東北線/高崎線 lines. It is a Service Pattern (rules.md §1.6), not an N02 railway, so it has no line row and needs no renderGroupId — it should only ever appear as a labelled service badge riding on those lines' own lanes, per rule R-09 and §10.
Same category as 湘南新宿ライン — a through-running service over 東北線/東海道線, not its own N02 railway; no package line row.

Also absent from jp-2025.json (searched: no line with this name or a 京浜東北 substring). Like the two services above, Keihin-Tohoku is a JR East commercial service brand riding the legal 東北線 (Omiya–Tokyo) and 東海道線 (Tokyo–Ofuna) tracks, not its own N02 railway. This matters directly for the 品川–田町 hub example in display-hubs.jp.proposed.json: the real 3-track order there is 東海道線 | 京浜東北線 | 山手線, but the middle lane's line has no package id to assign a lane to — documented as a gap in that hub's laneOrder rather than invented.
